subject: HealthBridge: session log purge windows & SOC 2 evidence request
messages:

Cc: Data Protection Team <dataprotection@healthbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on session log purge window + SOC 2 evidence

Hi Chloe,

Quick question from our Ops & Compliance team: we ingest user session traces routed through Redwood and a small subset of those traces (session-level metadata, timestamps, request IDs) are required to be retained for 90 days for forensic analysis by our incident response team. Our understanding from the standard Redwood doc is that session logs are TTL'd at 30 days in hosted deployments. Can you confirm whether HealthBridge can request an account-level exception to extend session log retention to 90 days, and what evidence you can provide for SOC 2/attestation that the additional data is retained only for that purpose?

Specifically we need:
- Confirmation if an account-level retention extension is possible on hosted Redwood.
- What controls/logs you can share to demonstrate retention/secure deletion (e.g., proof-of-delete manifests, audit trail entries).
- Any SOC 2 / CAIQ references that map to log retention and evidence items we can include in our review.

Thanks — appreciate a short turnaround; we're starting an audit next week.

Best,
Samir Patel
Data Protection Lead
HealthBridge Analytics

Marissa, can you confirm the policy/controls and what artifacts we can produce? Ben — please flag any operational constraints.

I can coordinate a single zip of artifacts for your audit if that works: retention matrix, example audit trail slice, and a sanitized sample of logs. If you prefer, we can also propose a short-term private provisioning for the extended retention window.

Next steps: Marissa to respond with policy & artifacts, Ben to confirm operational feasibility, and Chloe to set delivery timeline.

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthbridge.com>, chloe_martin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Question on session log purge window + SOC 2 evidence

Hi Samir / Chloe,

Thanks — I dug into the HealthBridge ask and mapped it to our internal controls. Summary below and attached a high-level "soc2-data-retention-matrix.pdf" that maps Redwood controls to common SOC 2 / CAIQ questions.

1) Account-level extension: possible for "session-metadata" and "session-index" (non-PII) on our hosted tier. We do NOT recommend retaining raw request bodies beyond standard TTL unless you have a signed Data Processing Addendum and explicit justification. Extension is implemented as a scoped retention policy (policy id: RBW-RP-EXT-2027-001) that changes the TTL for specified log buckets to 90 days.

2) Controls and evidence we can provide:
- Retention policy change record (policy id + effective timestamp) with approver audit trail.
- Audit log slices showing retention policy assignment to the HealthBridge account. Entries include actor, timestamp, policy_id, and expiry timestamp. (We can provide a 7-day slice as CSV).
- Proof-of-delete manifests for records deleted after expiry: a signed manifest (SHA256) and timestamped deletion job IDs.
- System access control listing showing which service principals can read raw session logs.
- Snapshot of our SOC 2 audit mapping for log retention items (see attached PDF).

3) Implementation variants:
- Hosted extension (recommended minimal impact): we keep logs in encrypted object storage for 90 days with strict ACLs, provide audit slices and deletion manifests. Cost increases are usage-based.
- Export-and-retain alternative (stronger isolation): Redwood can run an automated daily export of session metadata to a HealthBridge-owned S3 bucket; Redwood records the export manifest in our audit trail. HealthBridge retains exports for your 90-day window and controls deletion. This avoids long-lived retention on our cluster.

4) Limitations & notes:
- If HealthBridge uses Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), retention windows are customer-configured and Redwood will provide the same proof-of-delete tooling but cannot impose the deletion on your infra.
- We cannot produce raw payloads that contain third-party user PII without a data-minimization justification and explicit DPA amendment.

Attachments included: session-logs-sample.csv (sanitized), soc2-data-retention-matrix.pdf (mapping).

If you can confirm the scope (which log buckets and whether you need request body vs metadata), we will prepare the artifacts for your audit by EOD next business day.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthbridge.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Follow-up: operational impact and SLA considerations

Samir — a couple operational points from infra side before we flip the switch:

- Cost: 90-day retention will increase object storage and snapshot costs for your tenant. We can provide a cost estimate once you confirm average daily session-index volume.
- Performance: extending TTL on log buckets does not affect inference CPU/GPU, it's object store only.
- Recovery/forensics: we can provide a 7-day rolling window export by default if you want faster access to recent items and then full 90-day retention for deep forensics.
- SLA note: extended retention artifacts (manifests, CSV slices) will be provided via a secure link and retained for 180 days in our compliance archive for audit evidence.

Operational ask: please send a sample daily session count and a redaction list (fields that must be removed) so we can size storage and prepare sanitized exports. Once we have that, Chloe will confirm billing adjustments and Marissa will prepare the evidence pack.

Thanks — Ben
Director, Customer Security Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@healthbridge.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Data Protection Team <dataprotection@healthbridge.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on session log purge window + SOC 2 evidence

Thanks all — useful answers. Confirming scope: we only need session-level metadata (request_id, timestamp, session_duration, service_node_id), no request/response bodies. Average daily session-index ~ 120k rows (sanitized) and the redaction list is empty for metadata fields. Please proceed with: hosted account-level retention extension to 90 days + delivery of the PDF mapping, a 7-day CSV audit slice, and a proof-of-delete manifest for the first expiry after the 90-day window. We agree to the incremental storage charge; Chloe, can you confirm the billing cadence for the extension?

Samir
Data Protection Lead
HealthBridge Analytics
